title: survey.json
description: What a project is, as llocal's survey reads it: framework, pages, server routes, data, login, outside services and settings. llocal-survey writes it by rules; the builder's agent may fill the same file. Never put a secret's value in it: only names.

files.description: Paths inside the project, with / between folders.

method.description: Empty or left out means any method.

languages.description: Like typescript, javascript, python or html, most used first.

frameworks.description: Like vite, react, nextjs, tanstack-start, express, flask, fastapi, streamlit, or html for plain pages.

builder.description: The tool that made the project: lovable, bolt, v0 or replit.

recipe_shape.description: The shape named by a valid llocal.json at the project's root: the app already fits.

servers.description: Programs in the project that listen for requests. More than one means more than one app.

files.description: How many code files in its folder run on the server: not pages, tests, config or another server's folder.

server_pages.description: The server draws the pages itself (templates, Streamlit, Next.js server rendering or server actions).

pages.description: Pages people open in the browser.

routes.description: Server routes: the app's own API.

functions.description: Server code called by name rather than by path.

host.description: The database's address exactly as it appears in the code, like abcd.supabase.co or localhost:5432. The checker fails a converted app that still mentions it.

browser.description: Visitors' browsers talk to it directly.

env.description: Environment variables that belong to it.

file.description: Where the table is defined, or first used.

login.description: The app's own login, which llocal's sign-in replaces.

user_table.description: Where the people are kept, like auth.users or users.

services.description: Outside services that are not the database: payments, AI, accounting, text messages, email and the like.

name.description: Like stripe, openai, quickbooks or twilio.

kind.description: In plain words, like payments, AI, accounting, text messages or email.

browser.description: Visitors' browsers talk to it directly.

env.description: Environment variables the code reads or a .env file sets. Names only, never values.

browser.description: Its name has a public prefix (VITE_, NEXT_PUBLIC_, PUBLIC_, REACT_APP_), so a front-end build copies its value into the pages.

set.description: A value for it is in the project, in a .env file.

looks.description: What its value, or failing that its name, looks like.

service.description: What it belongs to: a service or data store name, login, or platform for names the old host or llocal sets.

keys.description: Keys written into the code itself. The value is never recorded.

schedules.description: Timed work: a timer or cron library in the code, or a host's cron entry.

webhooks.description: Routes or functions an outside service calls.

uploads.description: Places people upload files, and where the files go.

private.description: Addresses on a private network, or on localhost in code that runs in the browser.

unlisted_packages.description: Python packages the code imports, when there is no requirements file.

incomplete.description: Why only part of the project was read, when a cap was reached.
